subject: Estimator for non-normal and non-linear data

messages.author: 8a28755d4e2199e9
messages.subject: Estimator for non-normal and non-linear data
parts:
Dear all,

I was wondering if anyone could comment on the most appropriate estimator for structrual equation modelling with non-normal and non-linear data?

Thank you very much.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimator for non-normal and non-linear data
parts: I was wondering if anyone could comment on the most appropriate estimator for structrual equation modelling with non-normal and non-linear data?

You can find robust options on the ?lavOptions help page.  The Satorra-Bentler scaled correction for chi-squared is available for non-normal continuous complete data:

lavaan(..., test = "Satorra.Bentler")

If you have missing data and use FIML to incorporate all available information, you can request the asymptotically equivalent Yuan-Bentler T2* statistic:

lavaan(..., test = "Yuan.Bentler", missing = "fiml")

Note that the Yuan-Bentler statistic works fine with complete data.  If you compare models for which robust test statistics were requested, the anova() and lavTestLRT() functions will automatically detect this and calculate the appropriate (e.g., scaled) chi-squared difference test.  Robust SEs can be requested as well, for tests of individual parameters:

lavaan(..., se = "robust.sem")

or sandwich-estimator-style, which also works with missing data:

lavaan(..., se = "robust.huber.white")

If you like the sometimes-misleading Mplus keywords as shortcuts, you can request both in one step using 

lavaan(..., estimator = "MLM")

with complete data, or with missing data:

lavaan(..., estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml")

The only nonlinear link functions available are the probit and logit links for binary or ordinal data, which also require using DLWS estimation with robust SEs and a scaled/shifted test statistic ("WLSMV" in Mplus-speak).  Any other nonlinearity would require special tools.  Because your only categorical variable is gender, it is presumably exogenous in your model, so you can treat a gender dummy code as a fixed predictor by setting fixed.x = TRUE (the default setting).

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
